tob-10418: On a battlefield between two armies, the warrior Arjuna asks the god Krishna how he can fight without betraying his conscience. Krishna’s answer — to do one’s duty with a selfless heart — forms the heart of Hindu philosophy. Edwin Arnold’s verse translation, called The Song Celestial, brought this scripture to the English-speaking world in 1885. It remains one of the most beloved religious poems ever written.
tob-10818: Lewis Spence’s introduction surveys the myths of the world — Greek, Norse, Egyptian, Celtic, and the Americas — asking what myths are and why peoples tell them. He examines theories of myth from early folklore studies and retells the great stories with a storyteller’s flair. The book remains an inviting first step into the study of mythology.
tob-0118: Set down in 1797, John Robison’s scare-book held that the Bavarian Illuminati had lived through suppression and were quietly steering the French upheaval. A Scots teacher of nature-lore, he stitched hearsay into a grand plot-theory. The book sired the modern shelf of conspiracy writing.
tob-4118: Stephen MacKenna’s Plotinus — finished by B. S. Page — gives English readers the Enneads, the ground-book of latter-day Platonism. His vision of the soul’s climb to the One fed Christian and Muslim holy men. The edition is the classic English Plotinus.
cia-0000103318: An August 1989 report on Iraq's push to cut down its foreign workforce. Millions of guest workers from Egypt and Asia kept Iraq's economy running during its long war with Iran. The document captures Baghdad, at war's end, trying to send those workers home — a policy shift the CIA watched as a sign of Iraq's postwar plans.
cia-0000104918: An August 1992 report describing a ceremony at Mocada Barracks — likely a military base marking an anniversary of its history. Such reports captured the pageantry and politics of armed forces abroad, details that told analysts about morale and loyalties. The thin catalog record keeps the fuller picture locked in the document itself.
cia-0000107418: From February 1983, a report with new information on South Africa's nuclear program and its suspected nuclear cooperation with Israel. The two countries were rumored to have tested a device together over the South Atlantic in 1979. The misspelled title belies a serious subject: two isolated states, one shared bomb project.
cia-0000112818: An estimated 1945 report on propaganda and subversive activities in Shanghai. The city was a nest of competing intelligence services — Japanese, Chinese, Soviet, and Western — each running influence operations. The document captures the information war being fought in China's biggest city as World War II ended.
cia-0000119718: A September 1956 National Security Council briefing on Soviet policy toward its satellite states. As Poland and Hungary stirred, Washington needed to know how Moscow would react to defiance. The briefing weighed the empire's options — tolerate, pressure, or crush — at the highest level of American government.
cia-0000132418: A November 1959 forecast of the Caribbean situation through 1960 — the archive's title runs the words together. Analysts were predicting a stormy year: Cuba radicalizing, neighbors nervous. The document is the year ahead, previewed: the Caribbean, on edge.
cia-0000135818: A 1954 cable to LINCOLN about a plot against President Somoza. Nicaragua's dictator was in someone's sights — again. The document is the plot, reported: the tyrant, targeted.
cia-0000135918: A 1954 cable to the senior representative in Guatemala City, explaining a failure to act — the truncated title cuts off on what. The field had not moved; headquarters wanted to know why. The document is the excuse: the inaction, explained.
cia-0000136118: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN responding to a reference about a sabotage operation. The answer to the sabotage question. The document is the response: the operation, addressed.
cia-0000136318: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN on the REELFOOT trip. The journey, noted. The document is the travel: the trip, reported.
cia-0000137318: The record of the 411th NSC meeting on July 16, 1959, with an attached NSC briefing — the truncated title cuts off the subject. The July council. The document is the meeting: the 411th, convened.
un-ga-res-a-69-18: Resolution A/69/18, adopted in 2014 during the 69th session. The eighteenth act. The designation and year align; the subject belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-418: Security Council Resolution 418 — the landmark mandatory arms embargo on apartheid South Africa, the Council's first binding sanctions against a member state. The catalog dates it 1978; the historical record places the vote in November 1977. The resolution is the embargo: the weapons, cut off.
un-sc-res-718: Security Council Resolution 718, adopted in 1991 — aligned. The post-Cold War Council at work. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
un-sc-res-1918: Security Council Resolution 1918, adopted in 2010 — aligned. The new decade's Council deciding. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
cia-0000136618: An estimated 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136618, date approximate. The circa set. The document is the circa: the dating, estimated.
plos-pone-0000018: A 2006 PLOS ONE study of the molecular pathogenesis and therapy of polycythemia induced in mice — the truncated title cuts off the cause. Too many red blood cells, made in mice, then treated. The paper is the model: the disease, induced — the therapy, tested.
cia-0000132618: A 1960 CIA file on Latin America, section 10: anti-communist sentiment mounting on the Havana waterfront — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The docks turned against Castro. The document is the sentiment: the waterfront, restless.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d18: Generalissimo Chiang to President Roosevelt, July 4, 1943 — Document 18. China's leader answered on American Independence Day. The message is the answer: Chiang, replying.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d118: President Roosevelt to Marshal Stalin, November 12, 1943 — Document 118. The president wrote Moscow. The message is the letter: the president, to the marshal.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d218: The ambassador in Turkey, Steinhardt, to the president, the secretary — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 218. Ankara's embassy reported widely. The cable is the embassy's: Steinhardt, informing many.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d318: The director of the Civil Affairs Division, War Department, Hilldring — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 318. The occupation planner's paper. The memo is the planner's: Hilldring, recording.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d418: The ambassador in the Soviet Union, Harriman, to the Secretary of State — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 418. A third. The cable is the third: the envoy, prolific.
neville-trueman-the-pioneer-preacher-a-t: W. H. Withrow tells of Neville Trueman, a Methodist circuit rider preaching on the Canadian frontier during the War of 1812. Faith tested by war and wilderness drives this earnest historical tale. A stirring picture of pioneer religion in early Canada.
military-reminiscences-of-the-civil-war-: General Jacob D. Cox continues his Civil War memoirs through the war's final campaigns — Atlanta, Nashville, and the Carolinas. A thoughtful soldier-historian, he writes with unusual fairness and insight. This second volume covers November 1863 to Appomattox. His modesty and judgment make this one of the most readable of all Civil War memoirs.
arxiv-2605-08818: The isoperimetric inequality — among all shapes with a given perimeter, the circle encloses the most area — is one of geometry's oldest truths. Dangyang He extends it to degenerate elliptic operators of Grushin type, a class of differential operators where the usual rules break down. The 2026 paper is pure analysis, carrying a classical inequality into rougher territory.
arxiv-2605-09218: Understanding a 3D scene means composing parts — this chair, that table, their arrangement — without training examples for every combination. Sagar Bharadwaj, Ziyong Ma, Anurag Ghosh, and colleagues do it zero-shot with agentic language models in Flame 3D. The 2026 paper is compositional 3D reasoning.
arxiv-2605-09618: Statistical scouting for AI debate finds cases that are debate-safe but not debate-useful. Julia Hu, Alfred Shen, and Kumar Lakshmipathi report the matched-ceiling study of open-weight LLM reasoning protocols. The 2026 paper is a reality check on debate-based AI safety.
arxiv-2605-09718: Multiscale systems — from molecules to climate — hide stochastic dynamics operating simultaneously across scales, and classical tools choke on them. Anan Saha and Arnab Ganguly learn those dynamics through normalizing flows. The 2026 paper is machine learning purpose-built for multiscale physics.
arxiv-2605-09818: Chronic diseases need fast control — compressing time-to-control saves lives and money. Prabhjot Singh, Abhishek Gupta, Chris Betz, and Abe Flansburg frame the clinical problem as reinforcement learning. The 2026 paper is practical medical RL for real-world chronic disease management.
arxiv-2605-09918: LLM advertising is coming fast, and data-driven research should initiate it properly — NaiAD. Yihang Zhang proposes the research agenda for the field. The 2026 paper is the serious business of AI ads, carefully planned before the inevitable gold rush begins.
arxiv-2605-10018: Mechanistic priors — built-in knowledge of how things work — guide sequential decision making; their value is quantified here. Itai Shufaro, Gal Benor, Shie Mannor, and colleagues measure it. The 2026 paper is decision theory on the worth of knowing the mechanism.
plos-pone-0003418: Archaeogeneticists tested a wild-cattle romance rumor in this 2008 DNA study. Europe's first domestic cattle came from the Near East, but some wondered whether they later interbred with wild European aurochs. Examining Y-chromosome markers in ancient and modern animals, the team found no sign of such hybridization, keeping the aurochs and domestic herds genetically separate.
plos-pone-0003518: Cell biologists caught a protein commuting between two jobs in this 2008 paper. TRAF4, known from immune signaling, turned out to shuttle in and out of tight junctions, the seals between cells, behaving as a dynamic scaffold. The discovery explains how one molecule can serve both signaling and structural roles at the cell's border.
plos-pone-0003618: Clinicians Bradshaw, Chen, and Fairley found a stubborn STI surviving standard treatment in this 2008 study. Mycoplasma genitalium persisted in some patients after the standard one-gram azithromycin dose at a Melbourne sexual health clinic. The cure-rate shortfall flagged a growing resistance problem in a little-known but common infection.
plos-pone-0003718: In 2008, Vollmer and Kline found some corals can fight back. Staghorn corals hit by reef epidemics showed natural disease resistance, the first evidence the coral host itself can resist. The finding matters for reefs in crisis: resistant corals could seed recovery.
plos-pone-0003818: Working alone in 2008, Guenter Albrecht-Buehler described a strange feature of mammal DNA. He found long stretches made only of G and A bases, pure GA-sequences over 50 letters long, and mapped where they occur. The census of these odd repeats raises the question of what, if anything, they do in the genome.
plos-pone-0003918: In 2008, Li, Dai, and Kuang tested three generic HIV drug combos in China. The multicenter study followed Chinese adults new to treatment on nevirapine-based regimens. Efficacy and safety were weighed for each of the three combinations. The results guide affordable treatment choices for China's HIV patients.
plos-pone-0004018: In 2008, Klyubin, Polani, and Nehaniv proposed curiosity as a design principle. Their information-based rule tells sensorimotor systems to keep their options open. Maximizing future information gain guides movement without needing any fixed external goals. The elegant principle offers robots and animal brains one shared steering logic.
plos-pone-0004118: In 2009, Fulton, Peters, and Perkins turned gene silencing on a horse virus. RNA interference treated respiratory alphaherpesvirus infection in sick horses. The EHV-1 virus causes breathing trouble, nerve disorders, and abortions. The RNAi strike opens a new veterinary weapon at last.
plos-pone-0004218: In 2009, Creary, Ulug, and Menzel linked a chromosome spot to fetal hemoglobin. Genetic variation on chromosome 6 shifted F cell levels in people of African descent. The 6q23 region tuned a sickle-cell protector. The new locus guides future sickle-cell therapies.
plos-pone-0004318: In 2009, a team built a much sharper genetic map for plants. New Arabidopsis advanced intercross lines powered QTL mapping. The recombinant inbred lines dissected complex traits. The new resource serves plant breeders worldwide. The lines help pin genes behind natural variation.
plos-pone-0356518: What makes someone in Hong Kong buy used clothes? This paper extended the Knowledge-Attitude-Practice model to map the determinants of secondhand clothing consumption. From environmental awareness to price, the findings show thrift shops and policymakers what actually moves shoppers toward pre-loved fashion.
plos-pone-0358218: Uveitis — inflammation inside the eye — can blind, and its genes are still being mapped. This paper combined bioinformatics analysis of uveitis-related genes with differential expression data from an experimental autoimmune uveitis model. The gene lists narrow the hunt for what drives the disease — and what might stop it.
plos-pone-0357918: Newcastle disease devastates poultry — and mathematical models guide the response. This paper added stochastic delay derivatives to an epidemic model of the disease, with stability analysis and approximation. The refined math gives veterinarians sharper forecasts of how outbreaks will unfold and when they will fade.
plos-pone-0357018: China’s portable energy market moves fast — and social media chatter moves faster. This paper used large language models to monitor public opinion from social media comments on the market. The data-driven analysis gives companies a live pulse on what buyers think, want, and complain about.
plos-pone-0358118: Dialysis patients depend on nurses in ways no existing scale captured. This paper developed and preliminarily validated the hemodialysis patient care dependency scale (HD-CDS). The new tool lets clinics measure real dependency — and staff their units to match what patients actually need.
plos-pone-0347018: Shared decision-making between patients and clinicians needs rigorous measurement. This paper tested the reliability and validity of the Korean version of MAPPIN’SDM for both patients and healthcare providers. The validated tool lets Korean healthcare assess — and improve — real collaboration.
plos-pone-0354918: Childhood immunization across Sub-Saharan Africa varies enormously — and understanding why matters. This mixed-effect count regression analysis measured the magnitude of childhood immunization and its associated factors. The findings pinpoint where vaccination campaigns succeed and where they stall.
plos-pone-0355218: Living historic neighborhoods must balance preservation with tourism. This comparative study of three Yunnan cases examined tourism image perception of historical-cultural neighborhoods under the HSSPR framework. The findings guide planners toward tourism that sustains — rather than hollows out — living heritage.
plos-pone-0355018: ‘Heartbreak and frustration’ — Ugandan healthcare providers’ own words on caring for pregnant women with sickle cell disease. This qualitative study captured those experiences. The providers’ accounts expose a system failing both patients and caregivers — and the moral injury of watching preventable suffering.
plos-pone-0354118: After a PFO-associated stroke and heart closure, patients wonder what exercise is safe. This qualitative study captured their perceptions of physical activity after the procedure. The patients’ voices reveal the fear and uncertainty that keep stroke survivors sedentary — and what reassurance they need.
europmc-pmc2820518: Chunks of mitochondrial DNA keep turning up inside nuclear genomes, like ghosts of ancient accidents. This 2010 paper surveys these molecular poltergeists, called numts, across sequenced nuclear genomes. The authors catalog how common they are and what they do. The study warns genome researchers that mitochondrial lookalikes can confuse analyses.
europmc-pmc2871118: Plant compounds credited with health perks must first reach the blood. This 2010 paper reviews the bioavailability of polyphenols, weighing the status and controversies. The authors ask how much actually gets absorbed and what that means for health claims. Their sober look tempers talk about superfoods.
europmc-pmc2875518: Surviving intensive care is only half the story. This 2010 cohort study tracks quality of life in the five years after intensive care. The authors find many survivors carry lasting scars. Their long view pushed ICUs to care about life after discharge.
europmc-pmc2891718: Aphids beat a top insecticide by copying a detox gene. This 2010 paper shows amplification of a cytochrome P450 gene brings neonicotinoid resistance in the peach-potato aphid. The authors catch evolution in the act. Their finding explains control failures in the field.
europmc-pmc2994918: Melioidosis lurks in tropical soil, and this 2010 paper maps its toll. The authors review 540 cases from a 20-year Darwin study of the disease. Their data lay out its many faces. The work guides doctors in the tropics. Rainy seasons bring the worst waves.
europmc-pmc3042718: Vitamin A science got an update. This 2011 review covers how the body handles vitamin A. The authors survey the latest findings on its journeys. Their overview guides nutrition science. Too little blinds; too much poisons. Liver stores keep the supply steady.
europmc-pmc6544318: The brain's outer sheet is organized in gradients - from raw sensory areas to the deep-thinking transmodal zones. This study found that in those high-level regions, the brain's physical wiring and its actual activity patterns drift apart. The uncoupling may be what frees abstract thought from the constraints of anatomy - the price and prize of human cognition.
europmc-pmc6558418: Immune cells and tumor cells alike navigate by sticking - and cell adhesion molecules are the grips. This review maps how these sticky proteins guide immune cells into tissues and tumors, and how cancers hijack the same grips to spread and hide. Because adhesion shapes both defense and disease, the molecules are promising drug targets.
europmc-pmc6627318: Cisplatin kills tumors but can wreck kidneys - acute kidney injury is its notorious side effect. This review gathers recent advances on cisplatin's kidney damage: the animal models, the molecular mechanisms, the warning biomarkers, and strategies to intervene. Protecting kidneys could let doctors push this workhorse drug harder.
europmc-pmc6637318: A flexible heartbeat - high heart rate variability - may signal a nimble mind. This systematic review examines the link between HRV and thinking skills: whether the heart's rhythm reflects cognitive health. The connection is real but modest, hinting that autonomic fitness and brain fitness travel together.
europmc-pmc6642318: Cells eat their own damaged parts through selective autophagy - but the cleanup must start at the right place and time. This study reveals how NDP52 and TBK1 team up to switch on the ULK1 kinase exactly where needed. The choreography of selective recycling is coming into focus.
europmc-pmc6651418: Quercetin - the flavonoid that puts the bite in onions and apples - may starve cancer's sweet tooth. This review details how the plant compound rewires tumor metabolism: cutting the sugar-burning pathways cancers depend on. The molecular case builds for a humble dietary chemical with anti-cancer potential.
europmc-pmc6652118: Cells detect invading viral RNA with two sentries - RIG-I and MDA5 - that look similar but listen differently. This comparative review dissects their structures and jobs: which viral signatures each catches and how they sound the alarm. Knowing both sensors sharpens our picture of innate antiviral defense.
europmc-pmc6707218: Tumors shed tiny bubbles - exosomes - that home to other tumors like addressed envelopes. Scientists disguised drug-loaded porous silicon particles in tumor exosome coatings, creating biomimetic carriers that deliver chemotherapy straight to cancer. The Trojan-horse trick packs more drug into tumors with less collateral damage.
europmc-pmc6723618: A torn ACL can end seasons - and the treatment choice shapes decades. This evidence-based guide weighs surgery against rehabilitation for anterior cruciate ligament rupture, mostly in young active patients. The recommendations help patients and clinicians pick the path with the best long-term odds.
europmc-pmc6735718: Genomes differ by more than single letters - big structural chunks move, flip, and vanish. SVIM finds these structural variants in long-read sequencing data, which can span the tricky regions short reads miss. The tool gives researchers a clearer map of the genome's large-scale reshuffling.
europmc-pmc6752018: Plastic piles up by the hundreds of millions of tons - and some microbes can eat it. This review surveys the biotech of plastic-eating: which bacteria and fungi break down which polymers, and how close we are to real cleanup. Nature's recyclers may help with humanity's messiest habit.
europmc-pmc6760118: mRNA medicines ride in lipid nanoparticles - but most of the cargo never escapes the cell's entry chambers. This study links endosomal escape of LNP-mRNA to its loading into extracellular vesicles bound for other cells. The handoff reveals where precious cargo is lost - and how to keep more of it.
europmc-pmc6773718: The vaginal ecosystem shifts dramatically during infection - and the chemistry shifts with it. Profiling microbes and metabolites in yeast infections, chlamydia, and bacterial vaginosis, this study maps the disturbed landscape. The signatures could sharpen diagnosis of genital infections.
gao-gaoreports-b-310018: A 2007 GAO ruling on a contract fight from The Protective Group, Inc., a firm that sells guard services. The firm said the agency's award was unfair; the ruling tests each claim and gives the final word. For the guard trade, rulings like this mark the lines: how agencies must run a clean contest for guard work.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-18: A 2007 Government Accountability Office report on the Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites — the weather satellites that watch hurricanes and storms from fixed positions above Earth. GAO found progress in the program but said improvements were needed to manage risks of cost growth and delays. The report warns that gaps in weather-satellite coverage could blind forecasters when the next big storm comes.
gao-gaoreports-b-299918: A 2007 GAO ruling on a contract fight from Nautical Control Solutions, LP. The marine-gear firm said the agency's award was unfair; the ruling tests the claim and gives the final say. For the niche world of ship-system deals, the published call is a useful marker of how GAO reads a bid dispute.
gao-gaoreports-b-299818: Tech titans collided at GAO in 2007 — Systems Research and Applications Corporation versus Booz Allen Hamilton, four case numbers deep. The combined ruling sorts the dueling protests over a major tech deal. When consulting giants brawl over federal work, GAO's call is the referee's final whistle.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1018: Tons of drugs kept rolling north in 2007 despite U.S. aid to Mexico's drug war — GAO's report delivers the frustrating math. The full study behind the testimony details help given and flow unbroken. The findings fed the bleakest question in drug policy: what if the aid works and the trade wins anyway?
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-818: Farm subsidies were leaking to the departed in 2007 — GAO's report says the farm agency needed stronger locks against bad payments to estates and the deceased. The findings expose the ghost-payroll problem. The report's rule is blunt: check the pulse before cutting the check.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-718: Freight's modal handoffs were clunky in 2007 — GAO's report says the Transportation Department could do more about barriers between truck, train, and ship. The findings target the seams where cargo changes hands. The report's pitch: smooth the joints and the whole chain moves faster.
gao-gaoreports-b-299518: Matthews Manufacturing doubled its June 2007 protest — two case numbers, one contract fight — and GAO's combined ruling settles both claims. The firm challenged the awards as unfair; the call weighs each claim to a close. Twin filings get one thorough answer from the bid court.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-518: The Energy Department's project habit needed fixing in 2007 — GAO's report says consistent rules would lift its project management across the board. The findings press for steady standards at every lab. The report's lesson from years of overruns: discipline is cheaper than rescue.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-618: Rust was eating the military in 2007 — GAO's report says corrosion needed top-level attention and real action. The findings put a staggering price on the rot. The report's image sticks with you: the war machine was literally rusting from the inside out.
openalex-w7204745618: Chemistry comes alive in the lab, but many Brazilian public schools barely have one. This study asks PIBID teaching supervisors, mentors of future teachers, how they view the use of chemistry labs. The authors probe whether poor facilities break the link between theory and hands-on practice. A grounded look at the gap between what science teaching should be and what school buildings allow.
openalex-w7204641318: Pregnant women and new mothers in mental-health wards need to be heard, not just treated. This literature review studies sensitive listening as a care skill in perinatal psychology: how clinicians truly hear women in crisis. The authors gathered eighteen studies on the practice. Gentle and serious, it treats listening as a clinical tool as real as any drug.
openalex-w7204265718: A false positive HIV test can shatter a life, and this article asks who pays. The authors study civil liability for misdiagnosed sexually transmitted infections in Brazilian hospitals, focusing on the doctor-patient legal bond. They trace how courts handle the fallout of a wrong result. A precise legal study of medicine's most consequential errors.
openalex-w7204280318: A school garden can teach science, feed kids, and include everyone at once. This article tells the story of the garden at Antonio Malan school in rural Petrolina, Pernambuco: its role in environmental learning, teamwork across subjects, and student leadership. The authors present it as a living lab. Warm and practical, it shows education growing from the ground up.
openalex-w7127098018: A 5-year-old autistic boy arrived at the emergency department in crisis. This case report shows patient- and family-centered care in action: partnering with parents to calm, assess, and treat. The authors drew lessons for emergency teams. A clinical story of care shaped around the child, not the protocol.
openalex-w7214936518: Better hydrogen parts could green the grid. This paper reports a nickel-ceramic layer that boosts solid-oxide cells which split water into hydrogen. The team grew the tiny grains by a wet-chemistry method. A stuff study of parts for clean hydrogen.
pmc-13461218: This 2026 qualitative study reports what care home staff experienced delivering Hospital at Home — hospital-level care given inside residential care homes — to older residents with physical deterioration. The staff's firsthand accounts reveal what makes the model work and where it strains. Their perspective is essential reading for health systems expanding home-based acute care.
pmc-13459518: This 2026 paper reports the first human trial of oral camlipixant, testing safety, tolerability, and how the drug moves through the body at single and multiple ascending doses. First-in-human studies are the cautious opening step before any efficacy testing. The results determine whether the drug is safe enough to study further.
pmc-13445618: In this 2026 wound-care paper, researchers tested a foam-forming hydrogel loaded with antibiotics on thermal burns, finding it reduced bacterial colonization and sped healing compared with standard care. Burns are highly infection-prone, so a dressing that both covers and treats is valuable. The study reports the formulation and results.
pmc-13458918: A 2026 cardiology paper introducing a novel direct transcatheter mitral annuloplasty system — a device threaded through blood vessels to reshape the mitral valve's supporting ring. Annuloplasty treats leaking valves without open surgery. The paper describes the system's design and early results.
pmc-13428618: A 2026 pilot randomized trial testing the Informed Health Choices–Cancer programme, which teaches people to critically appraise cancer-related health information. Misinformation thrives where appraisal skills are weak. The trial measures whether the programme actually sharpens judgment.
pmc-13562218: A 2026 correction notice for a paper on [FeFe] hydrogenases with modified azadithiolate bridgeheads acting as unidirectional hydrogen oxidation catalysts. Corrections formally amend the published record. This entry preserves the correction as the journal issued it.
pmc-13426018: A 2026 pharmacology paper on predicting human pharmacokinetics of antibody-drug conjugates — cancer drugs that link a toxic payload to a targeting antibody — using mice transgenic for the human FcRn receptor. Better prediction means safer first-in-human dosing. The transgenic model is the methodological advance.
pmc-13416218: This 2026 public health study examined factors linked to US adults prioritizing quick firearm access over suicide prevention. Ready gun access is a major suicide risk factor, and the study maps the beliefs and demographics behind the trade-off. The findings speak directly to prevention messaging.
pmc-13404218: A 2026 public health round-up — a news-style digest of recent developments in global public health. Round-ups collect the month's notable stories, outbreaks, and policy moves in one place. This entry preserves the digest as published.
pmc-13408318: In this 2026 retrospective cohort study, researchers took a snapshot of the UK blood donor plasma virome — the full set of viruses circulating in donated plasma. Donor blood is a unique window on population virology. The baseline catalog supports transfusion safety and outbreak detection.
pmc-13472318: A 2026 engineering paper on a soft ionic skin that achieves human-like tactile sensing by intrinsically decoupling force and temperature signals. Touch sensors usually confuse pressure with heat; this design separates them. The advance brings prosthetics and robots closer to real touch.
pmc-13392918: This 2026 exercise physiology paper measured how high- versus moderate-intensity exercise affects gut barrier markers and inflammatory responses in healthy young men. Intense exercise can transiently breach the gut barrier. The comparison clarifies the dose-response of exercise immunology.
pmc-13482518: This 2026 multicenter prospective trial (BMT CTN 1702) used biologic assignment to study donor-specific transplant outcomes. The trial design — assigning by donor availability rather than randomization — answers a practical question. The outcomes guide donor selection.
pmc-13431818: In this 2026 study, researchers explored the association between antidepressants, disease progression, and mortality in Huntington's disease. The neurodegenerative disease's psychiatric symptoms need treatment, but drug effects on progression are unclear. The association data are a first step.
pmc-13526218: This 2026 case report traced a patient's journey from stroke to the final diagnosis: cardiac amyloidosis. The heart disease masqueraded as a brain event. The case teaches a diagnostic lesson.
pmc-13449918: A 2026 pediatric case series on pulmonary tuberculosis masquerading as chest neoplasms. TB in children can look like cancer. The series teaches the mimic.
pmc-13448318: A 2026 conference abstract (RMTC-11) on reporting of CNS efficacy in clinical trials of NSCLC with actionable genomic alterations. Trial reporting standards were examined. The abstract calls for better CNS endpoints.
pmc-13525518: A 2026 dental materials paper on sepiolite and zirconia nanoparticles doped with erythrosine — adhesive bond strength and antimicrobial performance in primary carious dentin. The doped nanoparticles served two functions. The dual performance is the advance.
pmc-13517318: In this 2026 animal study, parity and caffeine plus PGF2α administration affected hormonal and behavioral changes during parturition in gilts and sows. The farrowing process was modulated. The findings inform swine management.
pmc-13507518: This 2026 exploratory study examined short-term associations of resistance training with inflammatory biomarkers and BDNF (the title is truncated). The lifting-brain link was probed. The associations are preliminary.
pmc-13481318: A 2026 imaging biomarker paper on intermuscular adipose tissue as a multimodality quantitative biomarker — evidence across metabolic, cardiovascular, and oncologic diseases. The muscle fat predicted broadly. The biomarker is the advance.
pmc-13489718: A 2026 case report of arch and frozen elephant trunk repair for aortic dissection in pregnancy with situs inversus totalis. The mirrored anatomy complicated the emergency. The case is the surgical feat.
pmc-13466518: This 2026 natural products paper isolated a tuna-derived compound as protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B and alpha-glucosidase inhibitor via activity-guided isolation (the title is truncated). The fish molecule fought diabetes targets. The isolation is the discovery.
pmc-13467118: A 2026 Polish study — the first molecular survey of equine adenovirus type 1 infection among horses in Poland. The horse virus's prevalence was mapped. The survey is the baseline.
pmc-13457518: In this 2026 paper, heterogeneity in health risk behaviors was modeled with a dynamic mixture model informed by textual occupational data. The job descriptions informed the behavior model. The modeling is the innovation.
pmc-13453918: A 2026 two-year dynamic radiostereometric study of glenohumeral stability during external rotation in Latarjet procedure patients. The shoulder's stability was measured precisely. The study validates the procedure.
